entries.subject: Inspectable collective planning and dense reference execution

fields.Acceptance requirement: `collective.rs` provides deterministic semantic `DeviceId`/ordered `DeviceGroup`, broadcast, all-gather, reduce-scatter, and sum all-reduce plans plus a stepwise in-memory executor. It is tested across 1–4 devices, empty/uneven partitions, narrow storage, trace dependencies, and validation errors.

Sequential one-through-four-device sum all-reduce executes existing plan actions through primary pooled peer copies and typed add kernels against the deterministic mock. Every CUDA and in-memory executor revalidates the exact deterministic plan artifact before allocation or action submission, so tampered chunks/actions/dependencies/ranges/cache identity fail before mutation. Other collectives, overlap, narrow dtypes, NCCL/process transport, and live CUDA validation remain pending.

Not claimed. Checked-in tinygrad evidence is reduction-driven `ALLREDUCE` in `tinygrad/schedule/multi.py` and naive/ring/all-to-all schedule selection in `tinygrad/schedule/allreduce.py`; it is not a distributed-process API inventory.

entries.subject: Static tensor sharding layouts and exact reference data movement

fields.Acceptance requirement: `sharding.rs` implements immutable replicated/equal-axis layouts over the stable collective device group; validates ordered exact dense shards; and has exact `shard`/`gather`/replicate/redistribute reference movement. Evidence: checked-in `tinygrad/tensor.py::Tensor.shard` and `tinygrad/uop/ops.py::_shard`; uneven axis dimensions are rejected exactly as tinygrad does. Static movement and collective-lowering decisions are inspectable independently of Graph/runtime execution.

`sharded_graph.rs` validates graph-bound local node wrappers and composes shrink/concat gather, explicit redistribution, local elementwise/select/movement, sharded-axis sum/mean, and rank-two matmul through the existing CPU/reverse-mode graph semantics. Terminal sum-all-reduce traces retain ordered rank-local partials as a separate CUDA provenance ABI without changing the ordinary CPU/autograd reference graph. Canonical schedule-buffer attachment, lazy multi-device realization, and non-terminal/multiple collective graphs remain Phase 3 boundaries.

`sharded_cuda_plan.rs` validates semantic-device/primary-owner/capability bindings and serializes local schedule/PTX cache stages plus trace-derived transfer/all-reduce stages without entering CUDA or materializing data. A terminal all-reduce carries exact ordered rank-local output descriptors; that order, the collective plan, and the logical stage identity participate in the cache key. Old serialized records without those descriptors decode only as incomplete data and reject before execution. It retains renderable static elementwise/select/cast, exact Neg/Abs, and static reduction stages; graph-specific unsupported renderer contracts remain typed diagnostics carrying the renderer reason.

Graph-derived local Add has cache/oracle evidence across 1/2/4 owners for F32/I32/U64, including canonical zero routes. Static-view cast, broadcasted boolean select, and exact I32/F32 `GraphUnary` Neg execute through the generic semantic Mock across 1/2/4 owners; Neg retains original view-source bindings, owner-scoped cache isolation, and logical zero-domain no-work behavior. Unsupported unary/dtype pairs remain typed diagnostics. Typed transfer→local composition substitutes exact descriptor-matched outputs into local inputs and preserves a validated dependency DAG; direct provenance fusion validates explicit external-materialized ABI order and has CPU-byte evidence for 1/2/4-owner axis→replicated Add, 2-owner axis0→axis1 Add, and zero-domain no-work execution. A validated terminal F32 all-reduce now constructs owner-bound streams/peer access/typed add kernels only after full descriptor and capability preflight, mutating the paired local buffers in deterministic group order through the semantic CUDA Mock. Capturing primary contexts, streams, leases, peer state, or a live multi-GPU/NCCL transport is intentionally unsupported; callers replay only the data-only logical plan after rebinding owners.

Typed graph-derived two/four-owner axis-to-replicated, replicated-to-axis, and axis-to-axis routes validate ordered owners, layouts, graph-buffer identities, dtype, and checked element/byte ranges before exact mock execution. Same-owner DtoD and cross-owner peer transfers retain deterministic route order; injected DtoD/peer failures restore external sources for retry, including composed local execution. Retained-allocator stat assertions, collectives, and live CUDA remain pending.

entries.subject: Dense data, scalars and shape validation

fields.Acceptance requirement: Valid/invalid storage tests

Adam/LAMB checkpoint restoration uses full-width bias correction and rejects a final `u64` step overflow before state or parameter mutation. Checked static `diagonal` lowers through permutation plus existing `StaticIndex` for signed axes/offsets, rectangular/batched/zero/Bool cases. F32/F64 CPU-JIT `exp2` is strict native lowering with a renderer cache-version update; narrow floats reject. `FileBuffer::read_tensor_file` bounds metadata bytes and item-size alignment before copying a flat canonical little-endian rank-one `TensorData`, including empty files. `save_tensor_file` encodes complete canonical bytes before exclusively staging and syncing a same-directory file, then changes the target only by final rename and cleans only its own failed staging. These are bounded host/static surfaces: no dynamic indexing, broad JIT transcendental family, mmap/lazy/device backing, or optimizer/device redesign.

F16/BF16 public sums accumulate and return F32. Checked `SplitSizes` drives static `split`/`chunk` solely through existing `Shrink` views, while checked static `unfold` creates only validated sliding `Shrink` windows; both preserve signed axes and zero-domain distinctions. `Graph::roll` validates static signed axes and cardinality before composing only existing `repeat` and `shrink`; flattened roll accepts exactly one shift, while zero extents and zero shifts reuse the input. `Graph::cumsum` is an inclusive checked static single-axis `PrefixScan`: integer/bool inputs use default sum promotion; F16/BF16/Float8 retain source dtype; scalar and zero-extent domains are exact. Its typed UOp/RGUA payload has CPU-oracle schedule/materialization/cache evidence only. Floating `cumsum` composes reverse-scan-reverse over the stored normalized axis and retains graph-on-graph seed edges; floating `cumprod` uses a compositional zero-aware reverse rule, while non-floating/Float8 scan gradients reject before derivative graph mutation. Fixed-size `masked_select(size, fill)` separately reuses boolean prefix ranks only as nondifferentiable control to route an explicit upstream cotangent to retained row-major source lanes. Mask/index control, padding/truncation/false lanes, dynamic cardinality, CPU-JIT, PTX/OpenCL/Metal/WebGPU, parallel scans, and replay widening remain excluded. `var`/`var_mean`/`std`/`std_mean` compose existing mean/square/cast/sum nodes with F32-or-F64 accumulation and checked correction; Float8 variance rejects before graph mutation. `ones_with_dtype`, `const_like`, implicit random-like helpers, and typed `randperm_implicit` reuse captured Threefry reservations. `StaticIndexGrad`, `StaticIndexUpdateGrad`, and `ScatterPositionsVjp` reuse normalized static maps or static scatter positions for bounded graph-on-graph reverse construction. Einsum removes presentation whitespace before the existing parser; rearrange accepts Unicode identifiers but rejects empty sides before mutation. Directional `isinf` composes canonical predicates with typed sign comparisons; `hardswish` uses its source-matching ReLU6 composition; empty `logsumexp` has its local `-inf` identity; and accepted tinygrad scalar dtype aliases normalize to existing canonical `DType`s. Static `tril`/`triu` mask final two axes and supply causal attention through the same select composition. UOp scalar literals validate exact dtype/width in direct and artifact forms, while pure Add folds only type-matched positive raw zero and retains negative-zero literals. These are static CPU Graph surfaces only: no new runtime/IR/backend, dynamic shapes, device lowering, effect indexing, or broad dtype claim.

Exact integral/bool UOp identity rewrites preserve floating signed-zero/NaN lanes; `TensorData::bitcast` reinterprets only equal-width canonical raw bytes. CPU float extrema retain the left operand on unordered/tied lanes, and softplus/mish/logsigmoid use stable finite-tail composition. Graph `any`/`all` have typed empty identities; `Graph::masked_fill` is only the existing checked Bool-mask `select(mask, value, input)` composition, retaining its broadcasting, promotion, trace, and reverse-mode behavior. Seeded Graph dropout reuses existing random/select operations. `SafetensorsReadLimits` bounds owned local reads before the canonical parser, while writes exclusively stage and sync a same-directory temporary before rename, clean their own failed staging, and never open an existing target for writing. `Conv1d` joins the existing static `ModuleForward` seam through its canonical NCL-to-Conv2d lowering and OIW state; `AvgPool2d` and `MaxPool2d` remain bounded seam members. `Schedule::validate` rejects noncanonical IDs/dependencies/consumer mirrors and invalid shared buffer descriptors before planning, realization, or capture; direct temporary planning and schedule-artifact decode use the same descriptor seam. These are bounded static CPU and artifact-integrity semantics only, with no new scheduler/runtime, trainer, device, dynamic-shape, or generic parity claim.

entries.subject: Static diag, native Sin/Tan/Cos/Log, and transpose-conv modules

fields.Acceptance requirement: `Graph::diag` accepts rank-one inputs only, checks `n + 1`/`n²` before graph mutation, and composes existing unsqueeze, typed-zero pad, flatten, shrink, and reshape for exact zero `[0,0]` and raw-dtype behavior. Strict CPU JIT lowers `Sin`, `Tan`, `Cos`, and `Log` only for F32/F64 with deterministic scalar/vector cache identities and captured replay reuse; F16/BF16 reject. `ConvTranspose2d::new_static` is graph-independent, its legacy constructor delegates exactly, and its `ModuleForward` adapter only uses the existing static NCHW Graph lowering with configured channels. No broad diagonal/indexing, native model/device, transpose-conv geometry, runtime/IR, or dynamic claim is added.

entries.subject: Static cumprod, native Trunc, and 1D transpose-conv modules

fields.Acceptance requirement: `Graph::cumprod` shares typed static `PrefixScan` Sum/Product payloads with `cumsum`: one checked signed axis, exact scalar/zero extent behavior, CPU schedule/UOp/RGUA identity, and source dtype retention including Bool; v11 PrefixScan artifacts decode as Sum and the effect envelope is v13. Strict CPU JIT lowers `Trunc` only for F32/F64 with exact signed-zero CPU parity and deterministic scalar/vector captured-replay cache identity; F16/BF16 reject and `Cos` remains unsupported. `ConvTranspose1d::new_static` is graph-independent, legacy construction delegates exactly, and its `ModuleForward` path only reuses the existing static NCL-to-2D Graph lowering with configured channels. Scan autograd/JIT/device lowering, broader transpose-conv workflows, runtime/IR, and dynamic claims remain absent.

entries.subject: Signed-zero Abs and atomic scheduler state

fields.Acceptance requirement: CPU `Abs` preserves a F16/BF16/F32/F64 input negative-zero lane, matching tinygrad's observable `x * sign(x)` behavior; ordinary finite, infinity, NaN, dtype, and existing Abs VJP semantics are unchanged, while Float8 remains separate. Every host scheduler validates the next `u64` epoch before state mutation, and `LrSchedulerGroup` steps cloned scheduler/optimizer candidates before one all-or-nothing commit, so any child error preserves all child epochs and learning rates. This adds no weak dtype, Float8, optimizer family, trainer, runtime, or device behavior.

Public `LiteralScalar::{Bool,I64,U64,F64}` lets `Graph::constant_literal`, `binary_literal`, and `literal_binary` resolve an untyped scalar immediately to ordinary concrete scalar `TensorData` against a strong peer dtype. Signed zero remains distinct while NaN identity is canonical; integer conversion uses the existing checked tinygrad-compatible wrapping route, F64 follows a float peer or F32, and bool-peer integers resolve I32. No weak `DType`, storage, UOp, artifact, cache key, explicit typed `TensorData` API change, runtime, or device behavior is introduced.

`ScheduledOutputs` preserves the existing checked one-output projection while allowing one static CPU `Sort` producer to own stable input-dtype values plus I32 indices. `argsort` selects indices and `top_k` uses checked slices of the pair; signed axes, direction, empty/scalar domains, raw dtype lanes, and tie order are part of the typed graph/UOp/artifact identity. Only the CPU interpreter materializes this pair; capture/replay, native/JIT, and device routes reject it before work. `TensorGuard` validates finite, nonnegative values and positive row totals as an input-value passthrough, and a session pending reservation commits an implicit Threefry range only after that guard succeeds. Static `multinomial` uses an explicit stream or that guarded implicit transaction: replacement follows normalized inclusive-CDF selection, no-replacement uses deterministic Efraimidis--Spirakis keys plus stable top-k. Guards, ordering, and sampling are nondifferentiable and reject capture/optimized/device routes; no host postprocessing or hidden RNG fallback is claimed.
Matrix/row/scalar cases

Static dense `full/zeros/ones/empty`, integer `arange`, `linspace`, `eye`, all static `*_like` forms, `randperm`, scaled/Glorot/Kaiming uniform/normal initializers, `one_hot`, and `meshgrid` are CPU-tested. The CPU oracle has a typed U32 Threefry2x32 core with checked source vectors, carry-safe chunk planning, and raw F16/BF16/F32/F64 unit-interval construction. `manual_seed` safely resets a mutex-serialized registry of captured per-device stream reservations; each implicit random node records its key/counter so replay is independent of execution scheduling, including `randperm`'s F32 random-key reservation, packed narrow-float, odd-word, empty, and cross-call accounting. Captured schedules retain a typed random UOp plan and serialize its exact reservation; graph-free interpreter and strict native C replay cover static uniform (F16/BF16/F32/F64), tinygrad's paired F32-source Box--Muller normal (F16/BF16/F32/F64), and the F32 uniform-scale-then-cast `randint` route for all public integer storage dtypes. Native rendering uses the immutable key/counter reservation only; it neither reads nor mutates the stream registry. CUDA PTX lowers captured static uniform/normal F16 (sm_53+), BF16, F32, and F64 plus F32-uniform-scale `randint` for every public integer storage dtype through immutable Threefry payloads and owner-scoped exact semantic mocks. PTX normal uses target approximate transcendentals, so live CUDA comparison is tolerance-only; no live CUDA/ptxas evidence is claimed. Accelerator state reservation and live accelerator validation remain explicit boundaries. Numeric device `0` uses tinygrad's first-device SHA-derived key; other numeric device IDs use documented deterministic distinct keys because RustGrad has no canonical backend-device name layer yet. Explicit seed APIs remain supported as a separate stateless compatibility contract. RustGrad `empty` deterministically zero-initializes instead of exposing allocator contents. Source-facing `Graph::full_tinygrad` accepts concrete Shape/Scalar plus optional local dtype and buffer flag: Bool/I32/F32 defaults, any local explicit dtype override, dense typed Constant `buffer=true`, or scalar-backed Expand `buffer=false`; established storage commitment retains integer wrapping and signed-zero/NaN/infinity behavior, including scalar/zero shapes and atomic extent preflight. Source-literal `zeros_tinygrad`/`ones_tinygrad` default to F32 or accept any local explicit dtype; `full_like_tinygrad`/`zeros_like_tinygrad`/`ones_like_tinygrad` default to the receiver dtype or override it. All retain the dense-versus-scalar-backed buffer boundary, scalar/zero/special payload commitment, receiver value/VJP independence, and atomic receiver/output extent validation. `manual_seed` safely resets a mutex-serialized registry of captured per-device stream reservations; each implicit random node records its key/counter so replay is independent of execution scheduling, including packed narrow-float, odd-word, empty, and cross-call accounting. `const_like` and current implicit/default `rand`/`randn`/`rand_like`/`randn_like`/`uniform`/`normal`/`scaled_uniform`/Glorot/Kaiming/`randperm` aliases are present. Source-literal `scaled_uniform` retains the complete `uniform(-1,1)` chain followed by a receiver-left `prod(shape)**-0.5` weak scalar multiply; positive shapes are clone-rehearsed before reservation, while zero products reject atomically because their source random request contains zero words and cannot change subsequent stream identity. Remaining boundaries are Invalid/live-UOp/device/sharding/symbolic-negative-shape `full` cases; deterministic-zero rather than uninitialized `empty`; arbitrary-precision `randint` bounds; live `random_bits`/`threefry`; device/live validation; and initializer families requiring SVD/contiguous materialization or sparse/convolution layouts.

entries.subject: Bool, integer, fp16/bf16/fp32/f64 and special dtypes

fields.Acceptance requirement: Dense tagged storage includes bool/i8-u64/f16/bf16/f32/f64 plus raw-bit-preserving float8 `E4M3`, `E5M2`, `E4M3FNUZ`, and `E5M2FNUZ`. **Float8 C6/C7 CPU oracle:** MatMul and Conv2d use their source-audited multiply-then-sum F32 accumulation with a single final narrow; Conv2d bias is then applied at its typed graph boundary. Static Einsum preserves raw storage for verified single-input diagonal-free reorders; its contractions use F32-step product/add accumulation and one final Float8 narrowing when the promoted result is Float8. Cross-format float8 and wider-float operands use the established promotion lattice. Homogeneous Float8 comparisons decode tagged lanes in the captured interpreter and CPU JIT while retaining raw bytes through affine views; homogeneous Float8 Select preserves the exact winning branch byte without a codec round trip; every other Float8 CPU-JIT ALU route fails closed. Accumulating scatter-add, padding, arg reductions, random, autograd, PTX/OpenCL/Metal/WebGPU/CUDA, and device ABI lowering remain fail-closed for float8. Dense tagged storage and a bool/i8-u64/fp8/f16/bf16/f32/f64 taxonomy exist. Concrete `DType` predicates, typed source min/max bounds, exact float8/F16/BF16/F32/F64 exponent/mantissa `finfo`, storage-backed scalar commitment, `least_upper_float`, the concrete lossless-cast matrix, and centralized sum-accumulator selection cover Bool truthiness, integer-width wrapping, float rounding, negative zero, and NaN; `ReductionDType` retains float8/F16/BF16 output narrowing after that accumulator selection. Host-only storage-scalar conversion and equal-itemsize scalar bitcasts cover current concrete dtypes, including float8/F16/BF16 storage, raw signed-zero/NaN/infinity values, and nonzero-byte Bool truthiness. Case-insensitive `DType::parse_tinygrad_name` admits exactly `bool`; `int8`/`char`, `uint8`/`uchar`, `int16`/`short`, `uint16`/`ushort`, `int32`/`int`, `uint32`/`uint`, `int64`/`long`, `uint64`/`ulong`, `fp8e4m3`, `fp8e5m2`, `fp8e4m3fnuz`, `fp8e5m2fnuz`, `float16`/`half`, `bfloat16`, `float32`/`float`, and `float64`/`double`; it does not trim whitespace or accept the internal `float8_e*` source names. `canonical_tinygrad_name` returns the corresponding inverse-dictionary alias, including the four `fp8e*` spellings; standard `Display` is the exact tinygrad repr `dtypes.<canonical alias>`, while `FromStr` delegates to that case-insensitive/no-trim alias parser and returns typed `InvalidTinygradDTypeName`. These remain separate from derived `Debug`/serde, source metadata, uppercase safetensors wire tags, and renderer/backend names. Const `tinygrad_priority`, `tinygrad_source_name`, and `tinygrad_format` cover all 17 concrete dtypes: priorities 0--8 and 10--15; float8 source names `float8_e4m3`, `float8_e5m2`, `float8_e4m3fnuz`, and `float8_e5m2fnuz` with no format; and the established integer and wider-float source names/formats. BF16 is `__bf16` with no format, distinct from its canonical alias. `bitsize`/`is_int` are source-named aliases; source-ordered `FP8_OCP`/`FP8_FNUZ`/`FP8S`, `FLOATS`, `INT8S`/`INT16S`/`INT32S`/`INT64S`, `UINTS`/`SINTS`/`INTS`, and `ALL` expose the complete concrete inventory. Public Graph convenience casts map checked-in `float`/`half`/`int`/`bool`/`bfloat16`/`double`/`long`/`short` to `to_f32`/`to_f16`/`to_i32`/`to_bool`/`to_bf16`/`to_f64`/`to_i64`/`to_i16`; each has same-dtype identity and the established typed-byte preflight/Cast semantics. CPU supports explicit casts and mixed binary promotion. First-class `Graph::bitcast` covers all 17 concrete dtypes with same-dtype identity, exact final-axis byte rescaling, raw-byte CPU/movement/capture/native-C materialization, nonzero-byte Bool normalization, and no gradient edge; nondivisible final-axis bytes and differing-width rank-zero values reject atomically. Strict TensorData Bool wire validation remains unchanged, while PTX/OpenCL/Metal/WebGPU/CUDA Bitcast lowering, weak/void/pointer/image/custom dtype names, complete tinygrad weak/generic promotion rules, and general device ABI lowering remain fail-closed.

Read-only concrete Graph descriptor queries include `len_tinygrad`: rank>=1 returns the leading extent including zero, rank-0 yields the typed source-equivalent rejection, and unknown IDs propagate. `bool_tinygrad` validates IDs first, then unconditionally returns the typed `__bool__ on Tensor is not defined` error for every valid shape/dtype without publishing a node or computing descriptor products or payloads. Overflow-shaped descriptors remain length-queryable without computing numel. No symbolic/device realization claim.

`TensorData::item` accepts exactly one stored element independent of rank and returns the typed `Scalar`; exported recursive `TensorList`/`tolist` preserves row-major concrete nesting and zero extents with F16/BF16 decoded through the established float conversion; exported borrowed `TensorDataReader`/`byte_reader` admits rank-one U8 storage, provides bounded `Read`/`read_to_end` and clamped `Seek`, and has no write interface; `replace` atomically swaps same-shape owned storage while allowing dtype changes; `assign`/`assign_from` perform source-order broadcast-before-dtype validation, exact same-dtype raw-lane broadcast copies, and transactional mutation. No live Graph/device realization API, borrowed typed memoryview/zero-copy data view, NumPy ndarray interop, gradient/device-aware clone/replace/transfer, weak/symbolic host values, or view-alias mutation claim.

entries.subject: Unary, binary, comparison and transcendental ALU

fields.Acceptance requirement: CPU primitives inventory includes add/sub/mul/div, neg, exp/log/exp2/log2, abs/reciprocal/square/sqrt/rsqrt, sin/cos/tan/sinh/cosh/tanh, erf/erfc, asin/acos/atan/atan2, asinh/acosh/atanh, copysign, relu, floor/ceil/trunc/round/sign, isnan/isinf/isfinite, pow, maximum/minimum, floor/trunc division, floor/C remainder, bitwise and/or/xor and shifts; comparisons, bool logic and broadcasted select are verified. Dtype matrix: predicates return bool for every stored dtype; float-only unary math promotes bool and all integer types to F32, while F16/BF16/F32/F64 retain and re-quantize their dtype; neg/relu/step/abs/square/rounding/sign retain exact bool/integer storage; binary operations use the checked-in tinygrad least-upper lattice (including signed/unsigned widening and F16+BF16→F32). Bool bitwise is AND/OR/XOR; shifts require a non-bool integer result type. Integer division/remainder by zero return `DivisionByZero`; signed MIN/-1 uses wrapping arithmetic. Shift counts must be `0 <= count < result bit width`; this deliberate CPU-oracle divergence narrows tinygrad's renderer-dependent out-of-range shift behavior. Float special values, inverse-function domains, copysign signed-zero/NaN semantics, and F16/BF16 construction/cast/unary/binary/reduction quantization are regression-tested. Float reverse mode covers smooth primitives (including special functions and atan2) plus pow broadcasting/zero guards and 50/50 extrema ties; copysign differentiates its magnitude only, matching tinygrad's predicate-based sign contract.

Unified static-axis sum/mean/product/min/max and argmin/argmax support all/signed multi-axis selection and keepdim, with CPU exact storage. Focused CPU regressions verify NaN-ignoring extrema, even tie shares, zero-aware product gradients, finite differences away from nondifferentiable points, typed empty sum/mean/product behavior, explicit empty extrema/arg errors, and `ReduceGrad` trace shape/dtype. Full tinygrad dtype-accumulation and dynamic/symbolic reduction coverage remain.

CPU-oracle generalized dense matmul supports rank-1 dot, matrix/vector forms, and broadcasted batch dimensions with promoted dense dtypes. CPU-JIT raw homogeneous F32/F64 Matmul mirrors the oracle contraction boundary: F32 rounds every product and running sum at F32 width per K step, while F64 remains double under renderer v16. `MatmulKernelPlan` owns normalized semantics; eligible nonempty F32 matrix forms carry a serialized deterministic `TiledMatmulPlan` and shared-memory PTX. Exact-tile homogeneous F16/BF16 matrices carry a serialized sm_80+ `TensorCoreMatmulPlan` with one-warp m16n8k16 row/col fragments, F32 accumulation, and one narrow-output requantization. Exact-representable simulator/oracle fixtures are covered; broad bitwise equivalence to the F64 oracle is not claimed. A separate `QuantizedMatmulPlan` covers F32 vector/batched activations times read-only Llama-orientation `[N,K]` Q4_0/Q8_0/Q4_K/Q6_K weights. Its independent reference and native C path decode blocks inside K accumulation, use f64 accumulation/final F32 storage, and never allocate a dense weight. K must be block-exact; K=0 is defined. Quantized backward, other formats/orientations, tiled quantized kernels, quantized PTX/device execution, tensor-core tails/multi-warp scheduling, empirical autotuning, and live-CUDA validation remain gaps. `MatmulGradVjp` retains dense second-order coverage; linalg beyond matmul remains.

CPU-oracle NCHW/OIHW Conv2d is acceptance-tested. **Static pooling is ✅ complete:** general trailing-spatial `max_pool`/`avg_pool` support arbitrary-rank options, including checked-in 3D tuple usage, and 2D wrappers delegate to the same normalized core. Generalized max indices return checked I32 flattened original-spatial indices with earliest-index ties; NaN, padding, dilation, ceil windows, divisors, and split-tie value gradients are acceptance-tested. Pooling behavior is validated from checked-in source and RustGrad's CPU oracle; only a live tinygrad runtime differential remains unavailable in this workspace. Winograd and broader convolution-family work remain.

Checked shrink/signed slicing, integer gather, deterministic replacement scatter, and scatter-add exist. `ir::indexing` provides typed immutable static mixed indexing (integer/slice/newaxis/ellipsis and constant broadcasted integer tensors), checked static sliding `unfold`, a narrow plan-carrying Graph op, CPU execution, and duplicate-accumulating F32 reverse scatter. `Graph::static_index_update` is a functional snapshot update with exact same-dtype RHS broadcasting and row-major last-writer-wins duplicates over bool/integer/narrow-float/float storage; its F32 VJPs use the plan's final-writer map, and `StaticIndexUpdateGrad` composes the same normalized static map for bounded higher-order seed derivatives. `EffectGraph::static_index_assign` carries that same normalized plan in typed STORE/AFTER payloads and atomically commits immutable target snapshots through `EffectRuntime`, including signed slices, advanced duplicates, RHS broadcasting, and raw narrow-float lanes. `EffectMutationPermit` performs a graph-derived first-order backward-slice analysis and binds a safe result to one exact target state: guarded whole, affine, and indexed effect assignments reject before STORE construction when the old pure value is needed by the requested backward slice; detached/no-grad, non-differentiable-only, and unrelated targets are classified safely. RGSM v2 serializes validated normalized index maps for graph-free interpreter replay against caller-owned effect state; malformed, stale, live-borrow, or injected failures preflight/abort without partial mutation, while RGSM v1 remains decodable. The permit is host/interpreter-only and is neither a persistent alias registry nor an effect VJP. Pure/effect mutation autograd beyond this static graph transform, native/device indexed-effect replay, and effect batches remain separate. Dense host `TensorData::assign_from` provides same-dtype whole-buffer broadcast assignment with snapshot source reads and transactional failure. `ir::dynamic` adds CPU-oracle `nonzero` with a typed rank/dtype contract and realization-time `[count, rank]` shape; its separately documented unbounded masked-select path is not a general dynamic indexing API. Static index values currently validate out-of-bounds eagerly, deliberately differing from tinygrad's zero-filled advanced-index read behavior. General dynamic boolean indexing and JIT/device lowering remain separate boundaries.

entries.subject: Mask, pad, concat, stack and split

fields.Acceptance requirement: Constant typed padding, multi-input concat with promotion, and fixed-size `masked_select(size, fill)` remain compatible. Its static reverse edge broadcasts/flattens the boolean mask, uses `PrefixScan` ranks only as nondifferentiable control indices, safely gathers explicit upstream cotangents for retained row-major lanes, and zeros padded, truncated, and false lanes; the mask and size have no gradient. The typed dynamic-result CPU oracle realizes `nonzero` and unbounded `masked_select_dynamic`, including checked bool-mask broadcasting and exact runtime shapes. `CpuSession` exposes the exact F32 masked-select route through an owned `DynamicTensor`: optional F32 `Neg`/`Square`, one checked static F32 scalar `Add`/`Sub`/`Mul`, and scalar `Sum`/forward-only `Mean` return detached CPU results. `DynamicAllocationPlan` and the canonical typed `MixedSchedule` retain exact runtime allocations, ordered bindings, lifetimes, and no placeholder capacity. Dynamic-to-dynamic binary composition, higher order, dynamic-session/dynamic-mean autograd, general dynamic Graph composition/`Graph::grad`, non-scalar broadcast, generic runtime-to-fixed consumers, capture/artifact/replay/native JIT/PTX/device lowering remain explicit boundaries. Stack and split remain.

entries.subject: Reshape, permute, expand, shrink, stride and contiguous views

fields.Acceptance requirement: Materialized reshape/permute/expand, signed `unsqueeze`/`squeeze`/`flatten`, compositional `stack`, checked shrink, signed stride, and reverse-mode movement mappings exist. Source-facing `Graph::contiguous` validates the full typed byte extent and elides only concrete Input/Constant/existing-Contiguous buffer identities plus their Reshape aliases; every other value emits a first-class non-fusible raw-byte owned-copy boundary. `Graph::contiguous_backward` is a forward identity whose VJP applies that contiguous contract to its incoming cotangent. CPU execution, producer-aware schedule dependencies, typed `MovementKernelPlan`, captured artifact round trips, native CPU memcpy/empty-domain rendering, all concrete dtypes including raw Float8 lanes, scalar/zero geometry, visualization, autograd distinction, and atomic malformed/overflow admission have focused acceptance. `ScatterPositionsVjp` closes second-order static shrink/pad/stride movement adjoints. Device-residency-aware identity elision and accelerator copy lowering remain boundaries.

Static dense `einsum` has a normalized inspected plan plus CPU forward and reverse oracle for arbitrary operand count, explicit/implicit output, ASCII labels, ellipses, repeated-label diagonals, broadcast-compatible labeled dimensions, scalar and zero-sized domains, and promoted storage. Float8 CPU einsum preserves raw storage for verified single-input diagonal-free reorders; contraction equations use tinygrad's aligned product then sum model with F32-step product/add accumulation and one final Float8 narrowing when the promoted result is Float8. `EinsumGradVjp` reuses that normalized plan for second-order upstream and non-target operand derivatives, preserving diagonal and broadcast scatter accumulation. Third-order indexed-contraction derivatives remain an explicit boundary. Static `rearrange` supports tinygrad's one-arrow identifier grammar with whitespace, `() / 1` singleton axes, non-nested parenthesized split/merge groups, Unicode/ASCII ellipsis, and named static factors (one inferred group factor); it lowers to reshape/permute and inherits their reverse mode. `repeat`/`tile` and scalar-count `repeat_interleave` lower through reshape/expand, including zero repetitions and gradient accumulation. Per-element repeat tensors and symbolic/dynamic output lengths, nested groups, and remaining rearrange features are unimplemented. Stable `logsumexp`, `softmax`, `log_softmax`, and compositional scaled dot-product attention support signed/static axes, narrow-float calculation control, bool/additive/causal masks, and static GQA head replication with first-order reverse mode. Training dropout supports inverted scaling through an explicit `dropout_seed`; eval mode bypasses it.

Portable checked little-endian dense bytes and safetensors state dictionaries (in-memory and atomic filesystem APIs) are implemented. Float8 `E4M3`, `E5M2`, `E4M3FNUZ`, and `E5M2FNUZ` are dense `TensorData` storage/transport dtypes with exact raw payload retention; only standard E4M3/E5M2 safetensors tags are emitted, while FNUZ and all NPY float8 descriptors reject. `MappedTensor` is a typed immutable Unix file-mapping source with refcounted backing identity and checked byte windows; CPU/artifact/capture callers must materialize an independent owned `TensorData`, so it provides no zero-copy compute, mutable aliasing, device backing, or autograd alias semantics. Fail-closed Torch ZIP and legacy ustar TAR state-dict importers accept bounded protocol-2 CPU dense tensors through a no-code-execution pickle whitelist, retaining raw storage bits and validating non-overlapping stride reconstruction before materialization. `TorchStateReadLimits` adds bounded local ZIP-state reads and strict preconfigured-module loading through the existing all-lock transaction. `interop::host` provides dtype-agnostic signed-stride descriptors plus lifetime/Arc-bound read views and lifetime-bound injective write views without pointer or capacity escape. Canonical little-endian host bytes copy in row-major logical order to independent `TensorData` and transactionally from it, preserving raw bool/integer/float bits including narrow floats, NaNs, and signed zero. Its deterministic copy-based NPY v1/v2 encoder/decoder supports C- and Fortran-order materialized Bool, signed/unsigned integer, F16, F32, and F64 arrays; writer output is C-order little-endian. `load_npy_file_with_limits` bounds local file/header/rank/element inputs, and `save_npy_file` stages and syncs a same-directory replacement. BF16 and big/native-endian, object/string/structured/subarray/datetime/Unicode NPY descriptors fail closed. A bounded default-domain opset-13 ONNX CPU inference slice lowers concrete initializers and embedded tensor attributes; common arithmetic, predicates, selection and unary math; static Clip and inference-only no-op Dropout; Shape, Expand, Tile, same-rank constant-index Gather, constant-control Slice, positive constant-mode Pad, ConstantOfShape, static ReduceSum/Mean/Prod/Min/Max, and first-tie ArgMax/ArgMin; static NCHW 2D Conv; inference-only BatchNormalization; GlobalAveragePool; and static 2D float MaxPool/AveragePool. Local ONNX file workflows bound model reads, require exact named NPY input schemas before CPU execution, and stage selected named NPY outputs. Dynamic/control-flow/custom-domain, external data, dynamic indexing/pads/slices/reduction axes, Pad crop/reflect/edge, general-rank Gather, last-tie ArgMin/ArgMax, MaxPool index outputs/storage-order variants, BatchNormalization training/stat outputs, nonzero/training Dropout, CUDA/sparse/quantized/custom objects, NumPy/DLPack, device/mmap-backed tensors, and autograd alias semantics remain separate boundaries.

entries.subject: Universal IR for ALU, memory, ranges and control

entries.subject: Symbolic integers, variables, bounds and shapes

entries.subject: Memory planning, reuse, subbuffers and alias safety

fields.Acceptance requirement: `MemoryPlan` has deterministic checked HostDense temporary lifetimes and exact-compatible reuse, while generation-checked HostSlot leases prevent stale logical views. `EffectPlan` and canonical UOp STORE/AFTER lower whole-buffer CPU assignments into deterministic effect-boundary `ScheduleItem`s. `EffectRuntime` owns HostSlot-backed logical buffer generations and atomically commits fully preflighted assignments from immutable snapshots; raw dtype, empty sentinel, chain, diamond, stale, and retry cases are tested. Typed `schedule::mixed` bindings feed pure outputs and versioned persistent snapshots, including checked signed `AffineView` reads, into the same transaction. `CapturedMixedSchedule` retains bounded/checksummed RGSM state/value ABI sidecars. `CapturedMixedBatch` has graph-free in-memory interpreter and strict-native CPU ordered replay: all captures stage rebased candidates privately and one `EffectRuntime::execute_batch` commit makes final states visible together. Batch serialization, devices, mutation autograd/live-use rules, and invalid rebinding schemas remain boundaries; validated total/bijective descriptor/version-compatible rebinding is released. Native traces exclude runtime slots, generations, pointers, and bytes. Ordinary RGSA artifacts still reject effects. Canonical signed `AffineView` carries ordinary late-IR views and checked negative-stride effect targets; writable maps remain injective-only. `AliasLivenessPlan` retains base/view/version lifetimes and never assigns aliases reusable temporary slots.

`RGMB` is a bounded, checksummed, deterministic ordered envelope of canonical RGSM entries. Decoding validates every embedded RGSM and the recomputed logical batch identity before interpreter or strict-native in-memory replay. `RGBS` packages exact version-zero raw `TensorData` beside byte-identical RGMB; its bounded decode validates the state frontier before a caller-selected validated total/bijective `MixedStateRebinding` atomically registers a fresh host `EffectRuntime`. The resulting bundle replays through interpreter, strict native, or the retained PTX semantic mock without state-byte migration or destination/runtime-resource serialization. A backend-neutral prepared-prefix coordinator drives OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU, and CUDA/PTX adapters, executing detached prefixes before one host transaction commits effects. There is no CPU fallback, device-resident persistent state, compiled-resource serialization, arbitrary historical/process-memory checkpointing, or live CUDA/toolkit mixed-batch evidence. F16/BF16 packed writes, F64/I64/U64, raw narrow indexed-duplicate source coverage, invalid/incompatible rebinding schemas, mutation autograd/live-use rules, and unsupported UOps remain gaps.

IR-to-IR transform covers current ALU, movement, reductions and first-order dedicated primitives. Source-facing `Graph::gradient` / `gradient_default` performs one target-pruned reverse traversal for an ordered target slice, preserves duplicate result aliases, admits connected concrete floating targets independently of RustGrad's leaf tracking bit, and returns one shared typed `const_like(0)` fallback per disconnected target. Custom seeds normalize equal-numel or broadcast-compatible descriptors to the loss shape; implicit seeds require a rank-zero loss. A cloned full candidate transaction validates every derivative and zero fallback before atomically replacing the live graph while preserving its no-grad mode. Existing `grad_with` retains its single-target explicit-upstream validation and `create_graph` control.

Broadcast/reduction and finite-difference checks exist, including selection gradients through value branches plus product/extrema gradients across multi-axis and keepdim cases; predicates are intentionally nondifferentiable. Sum/mean, zero-aware product, max/min tie routing, reshape/permute/expand/shrink/pad/stride/concat, gather/scatter-add and select value branches retain second-order graph edges. `ReduceGradVjp` preserves product zero-count branches and extrema upstream routing; `ScatterPositionsVjp` preserves static movement adjoints. Floating `cumsum` uses the compositional reverse-scan-reverse edge with normalized-axis, scalar/empty, and graph-on-graph seed support; product scans and non-floating sum scans reject before derivative graph mutation. Fixed-size masked selection routes explicit upstream value cotangents through a static boolean prefix-rank map and keeps graph-on-graph seed routing; masks, sizes, and the prefix ranks remain nondifferentiable.

Generalized `MatmulGradVjp`, normalized-plan `EinsumGradVjp`, `Conv2dGradVjp`, and `ConvTranspose2dGradVjp` provide inspectable second-order VJPs for their corresponding value contractions. Convolution VJPs reuse grouped stride/dilation/padding coordinate maps; transpose convolution includes output padding and 1D inherits the singleton-height lowering. Pooling is compositional: average pooling differentiates normally and max pooling inherits the explicit tie/NaN `ReduceGradVjp` contract. Compositional attention paths backpropagate through query/key/value and are covered by finite fixtures.

Gradient paths accumulate by graph addition. Inputs carry explicit tracking state; `detach` shares values while stopping its edge; `no_grad` is scoped per graph and panic-safe. Host-only parameters bind by stable identity/current version into graph-local captured leaves; old graphs retain old values, tied handles share one leaf per version, and optimizer gradients carry identity/version stamps. Host-interpreter `EffectSourceBridge` records graph-local frozen provenance and `MutationTapeRecord` provides first-order F32 local replacement VJPs for whole, injective signed-affine, and normalized static-index writes, with broadcast-reduced RHS output gradients and explicit `Graph::grad_with` handoff. Persistent leaf `.grad` buffers, `EffectGraph::grad`, higher-order/capture/native/device mutation AD, and global mutable aliases are not part of the static graph API.

Smooth unary/binary expressions, broadcasting, ordinary movement, sum/mean/product/max/min, gather/scatter-add, select value branches, generalized matmul/einsum, convolution, transpose convolution, compositional pooling, and fixed-size masked-select seed routing support graph-on-graph second derivatives. Third-order dedicated contractions/reductions/movement/convolution, broader masked-select differentiation, and replacement scatter remain explicit boundaries.

Verified for implemented ops. `CpuSession` is the documented CPU-only public workflow: it owns explicit Graph bindings and session-validated tensor handles, realizes through this oracle, exposes graph traces, supports the existing first-order pure gradient transform, and rejects non-CPU session devices instead of falling back. Its bounded Phase B delegates static `sub/div`, ReLU, matmul, signed-axis softmax/argmax, permute/transpose, shrink/signed slice, concat, and integer gather to the existing Graph contracts; the separate bounded F32 `DynamicTensor` route owns exact masked-select runtime buffers and its documented unary/static-scalar/reduction consumers only. Phase C adds `CpuModuleTrainer`: fresh graph per static F32-feature `ModuleForward` sparse-classification train/evaluate request, with integer token indices accepted only when the leading module is `Embedding`; evaluated parameter gradients use existing optimizer/scheduler ownership and retain inspectable loss/logits/trace/version metadata. `infer_module_cpu` shares that bounded leading-Embedding input rule and otherwise returns detached output, trace, and canonical version metadata without mutation. Strict native module inference remains F32-only. `summarize_classification` supplies pure first-tie predictions/counts/optional accuracy for rank-two F32 logits and integer targets. No generic dynamic or device session fallback, generic trainer/data loader, mixed precision, runtime module-name dispatch, or metric-driven scheduler stepping is claimed.

`CpuJitBackend` provides cached native execution for Graph outputs and a validated `ScheduleItem` seam used by serialized replay. Process-local compilation is keyed by deterministic rendered identity and repeated artifact replay reports cache hits. Scalar/contiguous-vector elementwise, reductions, and homogeneous F32/F64 generalized matmul cover zero domains, vector tails, broadcast batches, multi-item dependencies, aligned contiguous views, legal strided scalar views, and vector scalar splats; native `Neg` is defined for Bool as logical-not and for signed widths as modulo unsigned subtraction with a bit-preserving signed result. F16/BF16/F32/F64 floating `GraphUnary` operations use the strict scalar or scalar-per-lane path. Misaligned/non-affine views, native narrow/integer matmul, tiling, and target-ISA SIMD remain explicit unsupported/fallback boundaries. Scalar/contiguous-vector elementwise, reductions, and homogeneous F32/F64 generalized matmul cover zero domains, vector tails, broadcast batches, multi-item dependencies, aligned contiguous views, legal strided scalar views, and vector scalar splats. Native raw F32 Matmul rounds each product and running sum through explicit F32 temporaries per K step to match the CPU oracle; homogeneous F64 remains double, correcting the former double-accumulate/narrow-once divergence. Native Reduce includes Product with a typed one identity and multiplication, including Bool AND; Sum/Mean retain zero/addition and Bool OR. Raw extrema initialize from the first lane, retain leading-NaN and signed-zero first-tie payloads, compare Bool/signed/unsigned lanes at their exact stored type, and now render natively for Bool/integer storage. B2 VectorProgram fails closed for every F16/BF16/Float8 register producer or consumer, including Load/Store/Select/Cast when a payload type is absent; vectorized requests deterministically use the source-correct scalar-per-lane half decode/encode or Float8 comparison-decode/raw-Select emitter instead. F32/I32 Select remains B2-eligible. Full tagged F16/BF16/Float8 vector-register ABI and broad narrow-vector optimization remain unimplemented; this is a correctness fallback exercised by raw Select fuzz. Scalar and portable-vector numeric-to-Bool Cast use `!=0` source truthiness, including fractional, NaN, and infinity values. Raw GraphUnary Neg/Abs uses exact storage semantics: raw Bool Neg is logical-not and Bool Abs/unsigned Abs are identities; integer Neg and signed Abs use storage-width wrapping, including signed minima and U64 above 2^53, never `fabs`/double. Raw integer Square likewise multiplies through defined U64 arithmetic before restoring the exact storage width, avoiding signed overflow and narrow unsigned promotions. Scalar and scalar-per-lane native lowering now admits storage-preserving Relu, source-predicate Step (including unsigned 0/1), Floor, Ceil, Trunc, deterministic ties-to-even Round with signed-zero retention, Sign, and typed IsNan/IsInf/IsFinite predicates; nonfloat rounding is identity and nonfloat predicates are exact constants. B2 remains deliberately limited to its proven Neg/Abs subset while all additional unary operations use the legacy scalar-per-lane fallback. Floating Sinh/Cosh/Tanh/Asin/Acos/Atan/Asinh/Acosh/Atanh use the C11 double math contract across F16/BF16/F32/F64 storage, while Erf/Erfc render tinygrad's deterministic A&S 7.1.26 polynomial and retain the same half-storage narrowing boundary. Raw `GraphBinary` Div/FloorDiv/TruncDiv/Mod/FMod distinguishes truncating division/remainder from Euclidean floor division/modulo, including signed-minimum divided by -1 and first-zero-divisor handling; floating lanes use widened C11 division, `floor`, `trunc`, `fmod`, and the oracle's ordered `a-floor(a/b)*b` formula. B2 retains the exact integer helpers, while floating division-family and extrema requests use the scalar-per-lane fallback. Computed affine movement rendering closes both its copy loop and kernel body, with balanced-brace structural acceptance. Native `JitBuffer` reconstruction preserves raw bytes and format tags for all four Float8 storages, including empty and special payload lanes. Homogeneous Float8 `GraphCompare` decodes loads/constants only at the comparison edge, preserves raw affine copies, and uses source unordered inclusive semantics; homogeneous Float8 `Ternary::Where` selects raw branch bytes without decoding or re-encoding; every other Float8 ALU rejects before native compilation. Float8 vector requests use the scalar-per-lane path. The renderer identity is `rustgrad-c11-scalar-v25`. Misaligned/non-affine views, native narrow/integer matmul, tiling, and target-ISA SIMD remain explicit unsupported/fallback boundaries.

Typed thread-confined instance/adapter/device/queue/logical-generation buffer/shader/pipeline/cache/command/transaction ownership; four-byte physical allocation with checked logical H2D/D2H and aligned D2D; bounded build errors; ordered storage-plus-uniform ABI; launch preflight; query and consuming collect. Static F16/BF16/F32/Bool/I32/U32 elementwise/views and staged guarded I32/U32 execution have deterministic WGSL and typed semantic mocks. The SDK-free loader intentionally rejects unpinned native callback/future ABIs before calls, so no live WebGPU evidence is claimed. Reductions, broader random storage, dynamic shapes, capture/profiling, multi-adapter execution, and broad live validation remain.

Checked owned file byte windows and deterministic null planning traces are tested; file-backed lazy tensors, mmap, and mockgpu/replay parity remain.

entries.subject: JIT capture, specialization, cache and symbolic replay

fields.Acceptance requirement: `CapturedSchedule` serializes concrete schedules or guarded static-rank symbolic families, then replays through explicit interpreter/native/fallback policy without Graph traversal. Executable RGSA v6 retains signed `AffineView` input descriptors for negative-stride replay and deterministically upgrades v1--v5 artifacts without weakening descriptor validation. Complete named bindings specialize checked UOp/schedule descriptors; canonical values key concrete specialization and process-local native compilation caches. Eligible specialized F32 matrix schedules deterministically retile and serialize the selection for PTX consumers; CPU native replay remains serial-K. Captured generalized raw F32/F64 Matmul retains renderer-v16 source identity and the per-step F32/F64 contraction boundary. Captured static-axis raw `ReduceFinalize` initializes extrema from their first lane and preserves leading-NaN/signed-zero first-tie payload ownership with exact Bool/signed/unsigned comparisons rather than a lossy f64 projection. Captured homogeneous Float8 `GraphCompare` decodes tagged lanes and retains source logical-not semantics for unordered inclusive comparisons; homogeneous Float8 `Ternary::Where` returns the chosen raw tagged lane unchanged. Symbolic batch preflight validates and compiles every invocation before execution. Elementwise broadcast, static-axis reduction, generalized F32/F64 matmul, source-backed affine movement chains, and exact-splat constant resizing are differential-tested for multiple legal bindings and zero extents. Dynamic rank/cardinality, arbitrary storage resizing, mutation aliases, serialized compiled code, live device resources, and CUDA graph integration remain absent.
Interop and lifetime tests

Graph-composed modules include `LayerNorm2d` and checked-in `LSTMCell` constructor/forward/state/autograd coverage alongside the existing normalization, convolution, pooling, and loss surface. State-free `ReLU`, `AdaptiveAvgPool2d`, and checked `Flatten`, plus graph-free `Conv2d`, `LayerNorm`, `LayerNorm2d`, `GroupNorm`, `InstanceNorm`, and `RMSNorm`, participate in the public one-input static `ModuleForward` seam: strict static `Linear → ReLU → Linear`, `Linear → LayerNorm`, `Linear → RMSNorm`, `Conv2d → LayerNorm2d → ReLU → AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear`, `Conv2d → GroupNorm → ReLU → AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear`, and `Conv2d → InstanceNorm → ReLU → AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear` fresh-state/inference acceptance are covered. `LayerNorm`, `LayerNorm2d`, `GroupNorm`, `InstanceNorm`, and `RMSNorm` preserve their existing checked rank/dtype contracts. BatchNorm's separate `ModeModuleForward` composes through explicit `ModeSequential`; its CPU `Conv2d → BatchNorm → ReLU → AdaptiveAvgPool2d → Flatten → Linear` workflow realizes output/loss/gradients/statistics before one atomic parameter-and-running-buffer commit, with detached optimizer/scheduler candidates. Evaluation is explicit and read-only. This neither changes ordinary `Sequential` nor adds global mode, generic trainer, checkpoint, native/device/dynamic, or mixed-precision training behavior. Other graph-composed Conv/pool/reshape/normalization/stateful signatures remain explicit. Tinygrad layout/init gates are tested; dynamic/data-dependent masking and remaining layers remain. The rank-two-or-greater `BatchNorm` implementation is publicly aliased as both `BatchNorm2d` and `BatchNorm3d`, with shared module/state semantics; no `BatchNorm1d` claim is made.

Static host `Muon` joins SGD/Adam/AdamW/LARS/LAMB with checked rank/float/config validation, momentum/Nesterov, and tinygrad-style Newton--Schulz matrix orthogonalization. SGD checkpoint restore preserves its dampening/momentum lifecycle rather than restarting the first-step rule. `OptimizerGroup` restores every child through candidates and replaces the group only after all succeed, so a late state or lock failure leaves earlier child slots and learning rates unchanged. Host MultiStep, ReduceLROnPlateau, CosineAnnealing, and OneCycle schedulers have checked state/config contracts. Existing optimizer checkpoints retain config fingerprints, legacy rejection, and strict expected-key loads; LAMB uses corrected bias correction. Fused/device paths, distributed state, and loss/gradient scaling remain. `OptimizerGroup` and host MultiStep, ReduceLROnPlateau, CosineAnnealing, and OneCycle schedulers have checked state/config contracts.

entries.subject: State traversal, safetensors, GGUF and checkpoints

fields.Acceptance requirement: Explicit deterministic `Module` traversal covers nested `Sequential`, buffers, tied parameters, strict/non-strict reports, fixed shape/dtype replacement, and safetensors round trips. `load_state_dict_strict` is validate-first and delegates successful candidates to the existing all-lock parameter restore transaction, so missing/unexpected/tied-alias-conflicting keys and shape/dtype/lock failures leave every visible parameter unchanged. Bounded strict safetensors byte/file helpers reuse the fail-closed decoder and retain exact keys, shapes, and dtypes without casts or heuristic remapping. The bounded in-memory GGUF v2/v3 reader preserves typed metadata, validates dense and quantized ranges, materializes exact dense storage, and dequantizes Q4_0/Q8_0/Q4_K/Q6_K.
